status: RESEARCH SHORTLIST ONLY; NONE IMPLEMENTED OR RUN; THREE-EXPERIMENT/TWO-HOUR BUDGET SPENT
novelty_scope: Compared with the inspected active anatomy implementation, archived experiment scripts, and the pre-merge H57 hypothesis slate in this checkout. Broad sense-by-angle/distance, slip-rate, tip-relay and junction-context ideas have already been proposed or partly measured; the shortlist does not claim global or repository-wide idea novelty.
ranking_basis: Qualitative next-test priority combines mechanistic fit to secondary strands, possible incremental signal, data readiness, and implementation cost. No numerical DTI gain or probability is supported. The expected-effect descriptions below are hypotheses, not results.
current_blocker: The independently SHA-verified 17GEMSDOE witness covers every allowable candidate cell within 3 px. Under the unchanged literal >70% overlap stop rule, the gate is unsatisfiable for any nonempty candidate while that witness remains in scope. The local public-registry cache is 0/679. Do not alter the gate, download data, implement, evaluate, or build a candidate without explicit protocol resolution and renewed authorization/budget.

data_audit.classification: Descriptive row/field inventory only; no host-level join, spatial feature, model, or holdout result.
data_audit.join_warning: Completeness in a CSV is not evidence that the attribute can be joined to a visible rasterized host without ambiguity or leakage.

candidates.hypothesis: Visible-host branch-end/junction topology—and its interaction with recorded slip sense—changes the fitted location and relative-strike distribution of nearby secondary strands.
layers: Visible-only fault skeleton/branch graph, endpoint and junction class/distance, local strike, cross-/along-strike offset, and component length from the competition fault raster/vectors
Recorded INGENIOUS trace-segment sense (`sense`: N, RL, LL, or unknown) from data/external/trace_segments_utm11.csv, only after a predeclared visible-host join is shown reliable
candidates.physical_signature: Fit class-conditional distributions for withheld-strand location relative to the nearest visible tip or junction: distance, signed normalized along-strike/cross-strike offset, and relative strike. Estimate only on training folds, shrink sparse topology/sense classes to a pooled fit, and impose no textbook angle.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: Splays and relay strands may cluster near visible branch terminations or junctions rather than uniformly along a broad halo. A fitted topology-conditioned neighborhood can allocate probability to off-trace geometry; recorded sense is only a possible stratifier, not a hard-coded stepping rule.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: The archived explore_zone.py/explore_zone2.py scripts measured d, relative azimuth, normalized along-strike position, length, and marginal sense-conditioned distance; the newer run_sense_experiment.py and run_orientation_experiments.py tested recorded-sense feature sets with existing geometry/orientation. The active feature matrix has no explicit visible branch-end/junction topology by fold. This is a narrower topology-conditioned refinement, not a new generic sense-by-angle/distance proposal or a claim of global novelty.
candidates.prior_work_note: An archived pre-merge slate (docs/research/hypotheses_h57.md) had already proposed generic tip-relay and junction/stepover ideas, but no result in that slate shows them implemented or run. The historical run_orientation_experiments.py also included sense with geometry/orientation; its recorded-sense comparison is HOLDOUT-DTI, evaluator gems57-pooled-hide-v2, 11,321 withheld positives, paired delta +0.003580783591493636, 95% CI [-0.005722027160876473, 0.014532120997528746], and sense was not retained. Do not present generic sense conditioning or a generic relay idea as novel; only this explicit visible-topology × sense-stratified fit remains untested in the inspected code.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Raster fragmentation, cartographic line breaks, lithologic/dike contacts, drainage lineaments, and vector-snapping errors can create false endpoints/junctions or apparent sense-specific relays.
candidates.relative_expected_dti_potential: Highest relative priority in this shortlist because it targets off-trace secondary-strand localization; effect direction and DTI gain are unknown, confidence is very low, and topology/sense coverage may be inadequate.
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium-high; reconstruct endpoint/junction topology from each visible-only holdout mask, test raster fragmentation and boundary artifacts, validate the visible-host sense join, preregister class support/shrinkage, and run independent feature canaries.
candidates.data_readiness: The official fault raster and local vectors are present, but no endpoint/junction feature or per-fold topology inventory was audited. The 84,331-row trace CSV has 1,394 missing sense values; matching a record to a visible raster host is unverified. Row completeness is not a join.

candidates.hypothesis: Recorded host slip rate modifies the fitted radial/cross-strike width and decay of nearby secondary-strand anatomy, beyond host length alone.
layers: Visible-only fault geometry and host length from the existing mapped fault raster/trace vectors
QFault/INGENIOUS `SLIPRTNUM` or its documented rate category `SCODE2023` from data/external/qfault_attributes.csv, only after a reliable host-level join
candidates.physical_signature: Estimate whether the distance-decay/width residual varies with recorded mm/year slip rate after controlling for length and fitted relative orientation. Treat slip rate as a measured rate, not cumulative displacement, fault maturity, or a substitute for displacement.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: If current deformation rate is associated with active secondary faulting, conditioning the width/decay of the halo could identify off-catalogue strands near hosts with different recorded rates; only held-out recovery can test this.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: The inspected anatomy uses connected-component length as a noisy host-size proxy; it has not used a validated host-level QFault slip-rate interaction. This is distinct from changing length's exponent or reusing the previously tested geometry-only model.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Slip-rate mapping effort, fault age/recency coding, uneven catalogue completeness, and lithologic contrasts may covary with assigned slip rate and mimic a physical width response.
candidates.relative_expected_dti_potential: Low to medium relative potential; the literature supports a displacement/damage relation, not a gain from present-day slip rate. Expected DTI change is unknown.
candidates.implementation_cost: Low to medium after a validated join; otherwise medium/high because attribute version, segment matching, duplicate records, and spatial leakage must be resolved first.
candidates.data_readiness: SLIPRTNUM is numeric on all 22,956 qfault attribute rows (84 distinct values, 0.0001–4.5 mm/yr). These are row-level counts only; no join to visible rasterized hosts was tested. The source field is assigned slip rate, not cumulative displacement.

candidates.future_test_gate: Pre-audit join coverage and missingness without holdout outcomes; keep length-only as the frozen comparator; fit one predeclared slip-rate interaction only on visible hosts; apply the full holdout, canary, CI, and registry protocol.
candidates.prior_work_note: Slip-rate-scaled damage-zone width was also proposed as H57-2 in the archived pre-merge hypothesis slate (docs/research/hypotheses_h57.md), but no model result there shows it implemented or run. It remains untried, not a newly invented idea; the current audit adds a row-level availability check and a stricter warning that rate is not cumulative displacement.

candidates.hypothesis: The recorded upper-bound recency of the most recent surface-deforming earthquake changes the relative distance/offset distribution of secondary strands around a visible host.
layers: Visible-only fault strike, distance, offset, and host length
QFault/INGENIOUS `RECNUM` or documented recency category `RCODE2023` from data/external/qfault_attributes.csv, only after a reliable host-level join
candidates.physical_signature: Test a predeclared recency-class interaction with the fitted distance and relative-strike/offset distribution. Estimate both near/far and along-strike patterns; do not impose the sign of the effect or interpret recency as displacement.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: If recently surface-deforming hosts have a different distribution of mapped secondary strands than long-inactive hosts, a recency-conditioned anatomy prior could place mass on new nearby geometry without simply extending catalogue traces.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: This is a recency-by-anatomy interaction, not the global distance/length/orientation baseline, not a sense-only feature, and not the slip-rate interaction in candidate 2. The attribute is present in the table but has not been joined or modeled in this repository's inspected active lane.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Regional differences in dating, preservation of geomorphic scarps, erosion, and map compilation can make the recency attribute appear to predict trace geometry even when no physical strand-age effect exists.
candidates.relative_expected_dti_potential: Low relative potential and low confidence; no direction or numerical DTI gain is supported before testing.
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; requires robust recency categories, host-level join validation, and safeguards against class/survey-region confounding.
candidates.data_readiness: RECNUM is numeric on all 22,956 qfault attribute rows (67 distinct values; 88–66,000,000 in the audited file). The field definition calls it an upper-bounding time in years of the most recent surface-deforming earthquake. Row-level completeness does not establish a valid host join.

candidates.hypothesis: An independently estimated host-fault slip/dilation-tendency attribute modifies the fitted orientation/distance distribution of secondary strands around visible faults.
layers: Visible-only host geometry from the competition's mapped fault raster and trace vectors
USGS ScienceBase DOI 10.5066/P9YL58W6 Quaternary-fault slip/dilation tendency shapefile, if its fields and geometries can be joined to the contest hosts
candidates.physical_signature: Within an anatomy halo fixed from visible hosts, test a continuous tendency-by-relative-strike/distance interaction using the dataset's documented tendency fields; estimate the geometry from holdout training only and do not hard-code angles.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: A stressed or dilatant host may have a different secondary-strand neighborhood; the proposed modifier would rank nearby off-trace geometry, not merely rediscover the host trace. This is a structural-fault hypothesis, not a geothermal-resource classifier.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: Uses a separately published fault-segment tendency dataset rather than the already-tested 19-band geophysical stack or a scalar geophysical edge; no such tendency join or interaction is present in the inspected active implementation.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Stress-model assumptions, uncertain fault geometry, lithologic boundaries, and shared source-fault ancestry can create an apparent tendency/strand association without predicting a new fault.
candidates.relative_expected_dti_potential: Low and highly uncertain until contest-grid overlap and a leakage-safe independent join are demonstrated; no numerical gain is estimable.
candidates.implementation_cost: High; retrieve and receipt the official file, review reuse terms, inspect schema, test geographic overlap, transform/reproject, and validate the host join before any feature can be considered.
candidates.data_readiness: The official USGS ScienceBase DOI record is publicly viewable and lists downloadable Great Basin and INGENIOUS shapefile/KMZ archives. No archive was downloaded. Exact contest-AOI overlap, feature schema/CRS, reuse terms for this competition, and registration to the 100 m grid remain unverified; this is data-gated, not yet a viable model feature.
